chunks.arabic_text: يَرْوِي عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ، وَأَبِي جَعْفَرً، وَأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) (كَمَا زَعَمُوا لَا يُرْتَفَعُ بِهِ، وَلَا بِذِكْرِهِ، غَالٍ، كَذَّابٌ).

translations.en: He narrates from ʿAlī b. al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him), and Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) [as they claim he is not ascended by (?), and not by his mention (?), ghālī, a liar].

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitāb al-Duʿafāʾ* characterizes Furāt ibn Aḥnaf as a prominent Kufan narrator of the Imams, yet marks him with the dual critique of being *ghālī* (an exaggerator, often associated with the Ghulat sect) and *kadhdhāb* (a liar). This specific combination suggests that while he was a known transmitter in Kufa, his theological leanings toward exaggerating the status of the Imams, coupled with potential fabrication, led scholars to question the reliability of his *isnād* and the elevation of his reports.
en.seo_question: Who is Furāt ibn Aḥnaf and what is his status as a narrator in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.فَرَاتُ بْنُ أَحْنَفَ: Furāt ibn Aḥnaf, the narrator being described.
key_terms.كَوْفِيٌّ: Kufan, indicating his geographical origin and scholarly school.
key_terms.غَالٍ: Ghālī, an exponent of Ghala' (exaggeration in the Imams' status).
key_terms.كَذَّابٌ: Kādhhib, a liar, indicating a specific critique of his reliability.
